title: The Live Deadline
premise: Ulyana Eastwick, a former intelligence asset turned whistle-blower, has survived four years under four names by trusting no one and sleeping in shifts. When a real-estate listing exposes the interior of her safe house, she realizes the network that trained her — the Meridian Group — isn't hunting her; it's flushing her. Racing across three countries before the border checkpoint rotations bury her escape route, Ulyana allies with a disgraced archivist who holds the ledger of everyone she used to be. To end the hunt she must broadcast the training program's records live during a corporate gala, sacrificing her last identity to destroy the machine that built it.
about_author: Felix Halloran is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent a decade moving sensitive cargo through Eastern European border towns before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about people whose paperwork is more dangerous than their enemies.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Scrolling property sites at 3 a.m., she finds her safe house for sale with photos of her own kitchen, her own bed, a red scarf she burned months ago. The beat: cold recognition that invisibility was an illusion someone allowed her.

chapters.title: Four Names
chapters.summary: Flashback-woven chapter establishing her identities: Mara in Riga, Ines in Porto, Katya in Trieste, Ulyana now. Her POV, paranoid and methodical. Emotional beat: grief for the woman she was before 'the incident.'

chapters.title: The Agent Who Knocked
chapters.summary: A polite estate agent leaves a card under her door: 'Meridian Property Partners.' Ulyana's POV. She runs instead of packing properly, leaving evidence behind. Beat: panic sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Rotations
chapters.summary: Ulyana maps border shift schedules on a motel wall, discovering the rotation changes in eleven days — after that, her forged papers die. POV hers. Beat: a ticking clock made physical.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Introduce Tomas Reiner, disgraced former Meridian records clerk, living quietly in Ljubljana. His POV. He recognizes her face from files he was ordered to shred. Beat: reluctant curiosity curdling into fear.

chapters.title: What Tomas Kept
chapters.summary: Tomas reveals he kept one unshredded ledger: every alias Meridian ever issued, including all four of hers. His POV, guilt-driven. Beat: two hunters of the same truth circling each other.

chapters.title: The Incident, Part One
chapters.summary: First full flashback: the training exercise gone wrong, the death Ulyana witnessed, the order to forget. Her POV, fragmented prose. Beat: memory as wound.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: A gray sedan follows Ulyana from Ljubljana to the coast. She doubles back, loses it, but finds a tracker in her coat lining — planted weeks ago. Her POV. Beat: the past has been holding her hand.

chapters.title: Vera
chapters.summary: Introduce Vera Solheim, Meridian's elegant fixer, via her own POV as she reports to Director Ansel Kade. Vera argues against killing Ulyana: 'Let her run to the ledger.' Beat: chilling institutional patience.

chapters.title: Uneasy Alliance
chapters.summary: Ulyana confronts Tomas at knifepoint; he offers the ledger in exchange for being named in her testimony. Her POV. Beat: trust as a calculated risk, not a feeling.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Reading the ledger together: hundreds of names, four of them hers, each crossed out when 'retired.' Tomas's POV. Beat: horror at how many people were erased like her.

chapters.title: Kade's Gala
chapters.summary: Kade's POV. Meridian hosts its annual gala in Vienna in nine days — the same night the checkpoints rotate. He suspects Ulyana will come to him. Beat: predator setting the table.

chapters.title: Porto Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ulyana detours to Porto to retrieve a dead-drop cache under the name Ines and finds it emptied — except for a photo of herself sleeping. Her POV. Beat: violation deeper than surveillance.

chapters.title: The Handler Who Cared
chapters.summary: Flashback to Dario, her original handler, the only person who showed her kindness — and who signed her retirement order. Her POV. Beat: betrayal wearing a warm face.

chapters.title: Burning Ines
chapters.summary: Ulyana formally abandons the Ines identity: burns documents, cuts her hair, changes her gait. Her POV, ritualistic. Beat: identity as armor she can no longer afford.

chapters.title: Vera Makes Contact
chapters.summary: Vera approaches Tomas openly, offering him reinstatement and immunity if he surrenders the ledger. His POV. Beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Tomas Lies
chapters.summary: Tomas tells Vera the ledger is in Zurich. It isn't. His POV, terrified of his own competence at deception. Beat: a coward discovering courage.

chapters.title: The Incident, Part Two
chapters.summary: Second flashback: what happened after — the cover-up, the coerced confession, why Ulyana ran with copies of everything. Her POV. Beat: understanding that her whistle-blowing was always suicide postponed.

chapters.title: Zurich Diversion
chapters.summary: Ulyana flies to Zurich to sell the lie, planting forensic traces of the ledger in a bank vault. Her POV, playing a role one last time. Beat: using their methods against them.

chapters.title: Vera Bites
chapters.summary: Vera's POV: Meridian strips its Vienna security to raid Zurich. Kade grows suspicious; Vera insists. Beat: the hunters divided.

chapters.title: Six Days Out
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Tomas plan the broadcast: hijack the gala's livestream using credentials from the ledger itself. Her POV, detailed and desperate. Beat: hope that feels like mania.

chapters.title: Dario Returns
chapters.summary: Dario intercepts Ulyana in Salzburg — not to kill her, but to beg her to stop, revealing he requested her 'retirement' to save her life. Her POV. Beat: love and control indistinguishable.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Kade himself calls Ulyana: full pardon, new identity, the incident officially undone — if she returns the ledger and disappears forever. Her POV. Beat: the seduction of forgetting.

chapters.title: Sleepless Vote
chapters.summary: Ulyana nearly accepts. A night without sleep, walking Vienna, she realizes acceptance means becoming one of the ledger's blank lines. Her POV. Beat: choosing self over safety.

chapters.title: Tomas Taken
chapters.summary: Vera, unconvinced by Zurich, takes Tomas from his apartment. His POV, brutal and brief. Beat: the cost of the diversion lands on the innocent accomplice.

chapters.title: Ransom of Records
chapters.summary: Vera contacts Ulyana: Tomas for the ledger, exchange at the gala itself. Ulyana's POV, fury and guilt. Beat: the trap closes exactly as designed.

chapters.title: Counterfeit Ledger
chapters.summary: Ulyana builds a decoy ledger overnight, embedding a second payload in its metadata. Her POV, craftsmanlike calm. Beat: turning forgery — her oldest skill — into a weapon.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Quiet chapter: Ulyana sleeps for the first time in the book, two hours, dreamless. Her POV, elegiac. Beat: peace as preparation for erasure.

chapters.title: Gala Entry
chapters.summary: Ulyana enters the Vienna gala under a fifth name — her real one, Ulyana Eastwick, deliberately. Her POV. Beat: reclaiming identity as an act of war.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Ballroom confrontation: Tomas traded for the counterfeit ledger while Ulyana's payload uploads toward the livestream. Alternating POVs. Beat: everything balanced on a handshake.

chapters.title: Vera's Doubt
chapters.summary: Vera notices the ledger's paper is wrong — new stock, wrong watermark. Her POV, a heartbeat of hesitation. Beat: the professional's instinct versus the institution's blindness.

chapters.title: Live
chapters.summary: The broadcast breaks: training footage, the incident, the ledger scrolling across screens at the gala and worldwide. Ulyana's POV, detached awe. Beat: exposure as liberation.

chapters.title: Kade Unmasked
chapters.summary: Kade, cornered on camera, orders violence anyway; guests film everything. His POV collapsing from control to panic. Beat: power revealed as performance.

chapters.title: The Checkpoint Shifts
chapters.summary: Mid-escape, the border rotations change early — Kade's last lever. Ulyana and Tomas reroute through a freight yard. Her POV, adrenaline and clarity. Beat: the clock becomes the enemy.

chapters.title: Vera's Choice
chapters.summary: Vera catches them at the freight yard, gun drawn — then lowers it, handing over her access badge: 'I was line 212 once too.' Her POV. Beat: the system's instrument defects.

chapters.title: The Incident, Resolved
chapters.summary: Final flashback interwoven with the escape: Ulyana finally remembers the incident whole, including her own complicity. Her POV. Beat: memory reclaimed without absolution.

chapters.title: Border Crossing
chapters.summary: Using Vera's badge and the old rotation gap, they cross on foot at dawn. Her POV, stripped and exhausted. Beat: survival without triumph.

chapters.title: Aftermath Broadcast
chapters.summary: News cycle: arrests, denials, Kade's resignation, Meridian's slow dissolution. Multiple brief POVs. Beat: justice arriving partial and unsatisfying.

chapters.title: The Fifth Name
chapters.summary: Ulyana chooses to keep her real name publicly, testifying under it, ending the era of aliases. Her POV. Beat: identity as testimony rather than disguise.

chapters.title: First Sleep
chapters.summary: Epilogue: a year later, Ulyana sleeps through the night in an ordinary apartment; Tomas visits with coffee and news clippings. Her POV, quiet. Beat: the whistle-blower's reward is not safety but rest.
